title: [factory-setup-agent] Setup round 1: sandbox tier is static — this repository has no application code
body:
Setup phase 2, round 1 wrote a complete, schema-valid candidate design to `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/setup/`. The headline finding is worth surfacing before the trial runs, because it is not something another round can fix.

## There is no application here

`main` tracks 56 files: `README.md` (two lines), 23 files under `.factory/`, and 29 factory workflows under `.github/workflows/`. There is no `.cs` file, no `.csproj`, `.sln`, `global.json`, `Directory.Build.props` or `NuGet.Config`, no Dockerfile, compose file or devcontainer, and no CI workflow that is not the factory's own.

This is not a partial checkout. The default branch's root, read through the GitHub API rather than the working copy, is exactly `.factory`, `.github` and `README.md`. The repository is a fixture at its starting state — the C\# API its name promises has not been written yet.

## Consequences for the sandbox

With no project file, `dotnet restore`, `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` all exit 1 with `MSBUILD : error MSB1003: Specify a project or solution file.` So:

- `commands.install`, `build`, `test`, `run` and `seed` are all `null`, and `app_url` is `null`.
- `env`, `services`, `stubs` and `egress` are all empty — no code reads configuration, so there is no variable to supply and nothing to point at a service or a stub. No credential of yours appears anywhere in the design.
- **`tier` is claimed as `static`.** The runner's own `reachedTier()` returns `static` when install, build and test all have a null command, so the measured tier should match the claim.

The toolchain itself is fine and is not the blocker: `dotnet` is on PATH with SDKs 8.0.x–11.0.100 and ASP.NET Core runtimes 8.0–11.0 installed. Only the project is missing.

## What this means for the gates

Every gate currently passes vacuously, and that is the thing most likely to be misread as a green result:

- `bsf gates static` compares against `baselines.json`, whose `rules` object is empty.
- `bsf gates coverage` compares against `coverage.json`, with `high_pct: 0` and `floor_pct: 0`.
- `bsf gates tests` has no tests to run.

No role should report a change as verified by running it until the sandbox is amended.

## The amendment to expect

The first pull request that adds a `.csproj` touches paths recorded under `capabilities.not_exercised` in the candidate manifest (`**/*.csproj`, `**/*.cs`, `**/Program.cs`, `**/*.Tests.csproj`, and the rest). That change cannot be compiled, tested or started in this sandbox, so it should trigger an inadequacy report and a `factory-setup` amendment run, which will fill in real `install`, `build`, `test` and `run` commands and lift the tier.

## Also worth deciding deliberately

Because the codebase sets no precedent, the first change that adds code decides the layout, target framework, minimal APIs vs. controllers, test framework and nullable/warning settings for everything after it. Setup did not choose any of these — that is an architecture decision, not setup's to make. It is also worth pinning the SDK with a `global.json`: eleven SDKs are installed and `dotnet --version` resolves to the newest (11.0.100), so an unpinned project moves silently when the runner image changes.

## What was written

- `context/feature-map.md`, `context/runbook.md`, `context/fundamentals.md`, `context/history.md` — every placeholder replaced; tables left empty where nothing fills them, each with a note saying what was looked for and not found.
- `manifest.json` — validates: `bsf sandbox check` reports `valid sandbox manifest, tier static`. Five `episode` entries record what was tried, including why no commands were declared and why scaffolding the missing API during setup was rejected.
- `research-domains.txt` — `learn.microsoft.com`, `dotnet.microsoft.com`, `www.nuget.org`. Platform documentation for the toolchain that is actually present; the repo declares no packages, so no library-specific host could be named.
- No `stubs/` — there is no third party to stand in for.

Two deliberate omissions are recorded under `dropped`: the factory's own workflows (machinery, not the app's build) and the agent firewall's package-registry allowlist (already permitted; `egress` is scoped to hosts needed beyond the registries).
